purpose: Continuous code-quality audits for the Airbnb-transitions build. Runs after every feature/sub-criterion completes to prevent silent accumulation of debt across the 2-day team execution.

scope.applies_to: All tasks in the rp-transitions team — architect scaffold, Workers A/B/C transitions, polish pass.

cadence.definition: An 'audit firing' is triggered every time a worker marks their feature task as 'completed' via TaskUpdate. The team-lead detects this completion and dispatches the four-dimension audit pass against the worker's diff.

secondary_passes.scope: All four dimensions against the new scaffold files
Full-system pass — D4 (System-as-a-whole) is the dominant lens here

cadence.rationale: Per-feature cadence catches issues while context is fresh, before they compound. Daily/end-of-build cadences let weeks-old debt fester. After-every-feature is the tightest coherent loop.
cadence.do_not: Do NOT batch audits to 'end of phase' — that defeats the prevention goal.

mechanism.primary: Combination: linter/grep for mechanical + agent dispatch for judgment

mechanical.exit_codes: 0 = no mechanical failures; 1 = mechanical failures present (file remediation tasks); 2 = invocation error
mechanical.philosophy: Mechanical checks are deterministic, fast (<5s), and catch the obvious. They are necessary but not sufficient — judgment dimensions require an agent.

agent_dispatch.tool: Agent (general-purpose subagent_type) joined to rp-transitions team
agent_dispatch.input: scripts/audit.sh output for the relevant dimension + git diff of the worker's commit + 12-continuous-audit.json (this file) + 00-build-brief.md
agent_dispatch.output: Findings filed as TaskCreate entries (one task per finding) with subject pattern 'Remediate D{n}: {finding-summary}' AND a SendMessage summary to team-lead
agent_dispatch.philosophy: Judgment dimensions cannot be checked by grep — they require reading code and understanding intent. Agents fill this gap.

mechanism.combination_principle: Mechanical checks fire FIRST (cheap, fast). Agent dispatch is conditional only on the worker's slice having significant code (>50 LOC changed). This protects judgment-agent budget while ensuring any sizeable change gets a real read.

D1_code_hygiene.purpose: Code-level cleanliness — preventable issues a competent engineer should notice on review.

checks.name: DRY
checks.mechanical: scripts/audit.sh hygiene flags duplicate function signatures across files. Tighter check (block-level dupes) requires ast-grep — when present, also runs that.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reads the diff for near-duplicate code blocks (logic that differs only by literal values, etc.) and recommends extraction into a shared helper or modifier.

checks.name: singletons
checks.mechanical: grep -rn 'static let shared' Sources/ — flags every occurrence
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews each flagged singleton: is it justified (e.g., URLSession.shared bridge) or should it be DI'd through the ViewModel init?

checks.name: dead code
checks.mechanical: scripts/audit.sh hygiene scans for `private func X(...)` whose name appears only at the definition site. Xcode warnings (-Wunused-* family) supplement.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent identifies dead types, dead extensions, dead enum cases, dead Theme tokens (which mechanical checks may miss because cross-module references hide them).

checks.name: magic numbers
checks.mechanical: scripts/audit.sh hygiene flags `.frame(...)`, `.padding(...)`, `spacing:` lines containing 2+ digit literals AND not referencing `Theme.`. False positives expected on animation tuning values.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent triages flagged lines: layout magic → Theme tokens; animation magic → leave inline (acceptable per brief); ambiguous → ask in remediation task.

checks.name: commented code
checks.mechanical: grep for `//` followed by Swift-like punctuation (parens, braces, equals, semicolons), excluding `MARK:`, `TODO:`, `FIXME:`, `NOTE:`, and URL-bearing lines.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent confirms each hit is actually commented-out code (not prose-with-punctuation) and recommends deletion or conversion to TODO.

checks.name: naming consistency
checks.mechanical: grep for top-level decls starting with uppercase (non-camelCase). Flags violations of Swift's lowerCamelCase convention.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews semantic naming: are identifier names *meaningful* (not `t1`, `tmp`, `data2`)? Are abbreviations consistent across files?

D2_architecture_and_abstraction.purpose: Structural quality — boundaries, abstraction, dependency direction.

checks.name: cohesion
checks.mechanical: File size > 500 LOC is a weak cohesion signal (one file, many concerns).
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reads each new file: is it doing ONE thing? If a file has both a View and a separate ViewModifier extension and a free function, that's a cohesion smell — split.

checks.name: premature abstraction
checks.mechanical: Count protocol conformers; flag protocols with ≤1 conformer (unjustified protocol = abstraction without payoff).
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews each flagged protocol: is it justified (e.g., for testability via mock conformer that only exists in tests) or genuinely premature?

checks.name: missing abstraction
checks.mechanical: N/A — there is no clean grep for 'this should be a protocol/struct'.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent identifies copy-paste between modules that should be extracted (e.g., the same blur+dim modifier reimplemented in 3 places).

checks.name: module boundaries
checks.mechanical: grep imports in lower layers (Models/, Networking/) for upper layer imports (DesignSystem/, Features/) — flags violations.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews any borderline cases the mechanical check missed (e.g., a Networking type that secretly depends on a SwiftUI type).

checks.name: dependency direction
checks.mechanical: grep for cross-feature imports inside Features/ (Search importing HotelListings, etc.) — flags any.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews whether the dependency direction across the new files is sane (downward only: View → ViewModel → Service → Model).

D3_senior_judgment_and_technical_debt.purpose: Anti-patterns and technical debt a senior engineer would refuse to ship.

checks.name: anti-patterns
checks.mechanical: grep for `try!`, `as!`, `fatalError(` in non-test, non-preview code. Each occurrence fails the audit.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews each flagged occurrence: is there a defensible reason (e.g., compile-time-known invariant that must crash if violated) or should it be a `try?` / `Result` / `guard`?

checks.name: code smells
checks.mechanical: grep for funcs with > 5 parameters; grep for nested ternaries; grep for guard chains > 5 deep.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews each smell: is the function genuinely doing too much, or is it a bridge function where parameters are unavoidable?

checks.name: complexity
checks.mechanical: scripts/audit.sh judgment uses an awk parser to flag functions whose body exceeds 50 LOC. (lizard installed → use it instead.)
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews each long function: is the cyclomatic complexity warranted (e.g., a switch over many enum cases) or should it decompose?

checks.name: file/function size
checks.mechanical: find Sources/ -name '*.swift' -exec wc -l {} + | awk '$1 > 400'. Flags every file over 400 LOC.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews each large file: are the constituents cohesive (one type with extensions) or is this a bag of unrelated stuff?

checks.name: hidden state
checks.mechanical: grep for `static var` (mutable globals — fail). grep for `@State` in Features/ — advisory output (gesture/focus state is OK; persisted-business-logic state is NOT).
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews `@State` occurrences in Features/: per-frame intermediate (drag offset, focus state, transient animation values) is correct; commit-worthy state must live in the ViewModel.

D4_system_as_a_whole.purpose: Whole-system health — does the change integrate cleanly without regression.

checks.name: regression risk
checks.mechanical: xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -scheme ResortPass build (clean). Existing Maestro flows must still pass.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews the diff against the original brief: did this change introduce risk to features outside its scope (e.g., touched a shared component)?

checks.name: cross-criterion consistency
checks.mechanical: N/A — judgment only.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews the changes against existing patterns in the repo: same Theme.* usage style? same MVI invariant (private(set) state, send entry point)? same matchedGeometryEffect ID naming pattern? Same animation parameter conventions?

checks.name: integration smells
checks.mechanical: N/A — judgment only.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews coupling at module boundaries: is HotelDetailScene leaking implementation details into HotelListingsView? Is the dismissProgress binding plumbed cleanly or does it bypass the ViewModel?

checks.name: holistic flow
checks.mechanical: Maestro flow execution (.maestro/13-transitions-audit.yaml or equivalent) — exercises tap-to-expand and swipe-down dismiss end-to-end.
checks.judgment: Auditor agent reviews the Maestro flow log + screenshots for jank, missed frames, layout shifts, or behavior that visually deviates from the Airbnb reference.

definition_of_done_template.applies_to: Every feature/scaffold/transition task — architect, Worker A, Worker B, Worker C, polish.
the_template: 2. scripts/audit.sh hygiene {target} → exit 0 OR all findings filed as Remediate D1 tasks before marking completed.
3. scripts/audit.sh architecture {target} → exit 0 OR all findings filed as Remediate D2 tasks.
4. scripts/audit.sh judgment {target} → exit 0 OR all findings filed as Remediate D3 tasks.
5. scripts/audit.sh system {target} → exit 0 (build passes) AND Maestro flows for the affected surface still execute.
6. Self-attestation: worker has reviewed their own diff against D1–D4 dimensions.

7. Worker marks task completed via TaskUpdate(status: completed). Team-lead detects completion and dispatches per-dimension auditor agents per the cadence rule. Audit findings become new Remediate-* tasks that block final acceptance of the feature.
definition_of_done_template.block_until_clean: Feature task is not 'truly' done until all four dimensions have been audited (mechanically + by agent) and remediation tasks are either resolved or explicitly waived by team-lead with rationale.

remediation_protocol.finding_to_task: Each judgment-dimension audit finding becomes a TaskCreate with subject 'Remediate D{n}: {brief}' (n ∈ {1,2,3,4}) and metadata { dimension: D{n}, original_feature_task: T#, severity: critical|major|minor }
remediation_protocol.non_blocking_findings: Minor findings (cosmetic, single-instance) may be filed as 'observation' entries in ux-research/team/audit-log.md instead of new tasks — these are tracked but do not block the feature.
remediation_protocol.feature_acceptance: Feature task moves to 'fully accepted' state only after all critical/major remediations complete OR team-lead explicitly waives with logged rationale in the task description.
remediation_protocol.audit_log_path: ux-research/team/audit-log.md — append-only running log of audit firings, dimensions covered, findings filed, remediations resolved.

where_in_plan_structure.layer_1_top_level_json: ux-research/team/12-continuous-audit.json — THIS FILE. Master spec; canonical source for the four dimensions, cadence, mechanism, DoD template, and remediation protocol.
where_in_plan_structure.layer_2_inline_definition_of_done: Every feature task description (TaskUpdate description field) contains an explicit 'Definition of Done' block listing the seven items from definition_of_done_template — workers see them in their TaskGet output and cannot mark task completed without them.
where_in_plan_structure.layer_3_auxiliary_expansion: ux-research/team/09-auxiliary.md — auxiliary tasks (audit dispatch, remediation patterns, audit-log management). Workers and auditor agents read this for the operational mechanics.
